title: Unique centered identification between two supplied toric tower lifts
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $M$ be a fine monoscheme, and let $T$ be a normalized tower of length $n$ with a specified $e_0:X_0\simeq\mathbf Q[M]$. For any two supplied centered toric tower lifts $L,L'$ of this same datum, there exists exactly one family of sheafed monoidal-space isomorphisms between their levels satisfying the centered identification predicate of [def-trf-centered-toric-tower-lift-data]. In particular it fixes the specified base, commutes with the ordered arrows, preserves the actual monoid centers, and realizes to the prescribed scheme comparisons. Existence of the lifts is assumed, and no regularity or terminal smoothness is asserted.

source.place: Exposé VIII, 3.2.14--3.2.20, pp.105--106, with the saturated charts of 3.1.19--3.1.24, pp.101--102.

proof.text: Fix two supplied centered lifts L and L′. At stage zero their prescribed base equalities give the identification. The initial realization equation follows by composing their initial fields with the inverse of the specified base isomorphism.

source.place: Exposé VIII, 3.2.14--3.2.20, pp.105--106, with the saturated charts of 3.1.19--3.1.24, pp.101--102.

proof.text: Inductively transport the second center by the preceding monoscheme isomorphism. The pullback formula for ring ideals and the two center and realization equations identify its realization with the first center’s realization. Injectivity of the coherent ideal comparison identifies the monoid ideals. On affine charts extend the base monoid isomorphism to the identical saturated blowup charts P[I-a]^sat. The extensions and their inverses agree on the prescribed localized overlaps, hence glue. They are local and commute with the arrows.

source.place: Exposé VIII, 3.2.14--3.2.20, pp.105--106, with the saturated charts of 3.1.19--3.1.24, pp.101--102.

proof.text: The monomial chart comparison realizes the specified scheme isomorphism: both are over the preceding scheme comparison and agree on the original dense component tori. The schemes are reduced by the component geometry, and the normalized blowup is separated over its base. Thus equality on this dense open proves the needed scheme equality. All ideal and arrow equalities are retained at every stage.

source.place: Exposé VIII, 3.2.14--3.2.20, pp.105--106, with the saturated charts of 3.1.19--3.1.24, pp.101--102.

proof.text: Any other centered identification realizes at stage i to the same scheme map, namely the first realization isomorphism followed by the inverse of the second. On incident affine charts, linear independence of monomials recovers the monoid map from its monoid algebra map; prime inverse images recover the point map. Equality on chart refinements therefore gives equality of the sheafed-space hom maps. The hom maps determine the isomorphisms; function extensionality gives equality of the families. Hence the constructed centered identification is unique. Empty spaces, zero length and unit-center steps cause no exception.
